theMigration.numbering: 0012 is the next free number after 0011a_parcel_gate_verdict_excluded_kinds.sql, the highest migration on origin/main at the moment this PR opened (git ls-tree --name-only origin/main migrations/). P-252 adds one concurrently: RE-CHECK before merge.
theMigration.table: stage_run_records -- one row per (county, stage, sub-stage, run). Columns: id, county_fips, stage, stage_detail, run_id (nullable, references runs(id)), run_mode, started_at, ended_at, outcome, instrument_verdict, instrument_artifact_path, rows_written, rows_written_basis, manifest_pin, compute_cost_usd, compute_cost_basis, compute_cost_unmeasured_reason, operator_minutes, operator_minutes_basis, operator_minutes_unmeasured_reason, created_at, updated_at.
theMigration.threeStatesInTheSchema: CONSTRAINT stage_run_records_compute_three_states_check CHECK ((compute_cost_usd IS NOT NULL AND compute_cost_basis IS NOT NULL AND compute_cost_unmeasured_reason IS NULL) OR (compute_cost_usd IS NULL AND compute_cost_unmeasured_reason IS NOT NULL)); the identical shape for operator_minutes; plus compute_cost_usd IS NULL OR compute_cost_usd >= 0 so a measured ZERO remains a legitimate distinct value; plus operator_minutes_basis ? 'declaredBy' AND ? 'declaredAt' AND ? 'stopPoint', so a declared value names who declared it, when, and at which of the three stop points.
theMigration.otherConstraints: county_fips ~ '^[0-9]{5}$'; stage BETWEEN 0 AND 12; run_mode IN ('apply','dry-run'); run_mode <> 'apply' OR run_id IS NOT NULL; outcome IN ('running','succeeded','failed','killed','orphaned','refused'); outcome = 'running' OR ended_at IS NOT NULL; ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at >= started_at; rows_written IS NULL OR rows_written >= 0.
theMigration.identity: UNIQUE (run_id, county_fips, stage, coalesce(stage_detail,'')) WHERE run_id IS NOT NULL -- one record per stage execution per run; and UNIQUE (county_fips, stage, coalesce(stage_detail,''), started_at) WHERE run_id IS NULL for dry runs, which have no run row to key on.
theMigration.views: stage_run_speed (one row per county/stage/sub-stage, with the UNMEASURED counted in its own column), stage_run_speed_per_10k (the same normalised per 10,000 parcels, carrying parcels_basis beside the figure), stage_run_comparison (two counties, one row per stage, ratios stated from county_a's side).
theMigration.whyNewTableNotColumnsOnRuns: `runs` is one row per PROCESS INVOCATION, and the depth writers each open ONE run for a multi-city sweep spanning several counties -- so a cost column on `runs` would have had to be divided across counties by hand, and the only thing to divide by is the run's scope LIST, which is a guess about how the work divided. That guess would have poisoned the exact number the program is going to make the isolated-store decision from. `runs` keeps what only it knows (image digest, engine sha, execution identity, the SIGTERM/reaper lifecycle) and the new table references it by run_id.
theMigration.durability: Nothing in the migration's SQL references leases, so releasing a lease cannot remove a record. The test asserts this against the SQL with comments stripped, AND asserts the file still discusses leases in prose, so the check is about the SQL and not about a deletion.

theAudit.whatFailsTheAudit: missingStageRecords walks every run that has a termination_record, maps its phase through the stage map, and for a phase whose runner DOES write records, requires a record for every county the run's scope names. A county it cannot key (no county in scope) is reported in `unkeyable` rather than silently passing.
theAudit.whatIsCountedRatherThanFailed: a phase that IS one of the thirteen but whose runner does not write records yet goes to `pendingWriter` with its ownerRow (P-285). Failing a store for a writer that does not exist would make the audit red for a reason nobody can act on, and a gate that is red for no actionable reason gets ignored -- which is how the last four controls on this program died.
theAudit.theOtherBuckets: notAStage, phaseAbsent, unassigned (a phase known to be stage work whose stage cannot be read off the code -- currently p2-juris-containment), and unknownPhase (a phase nobody has ever mapped). theAudit.theReaper: reap.mjs closes every open record of a run it terminates, with stageOutcomeForExitKind so a killed run's record is never marked succeeded, and backfills compute costs whose metric was not yet published while the job was still running.

contradicted: Three things, recorded rather than quietly corrected. (1) MY FIRST COMPARISON WAS SILENT FOR A COUNTY WITH NO RECORDS. compareCounties read stage_run_comparison directly. The view is correct for the case F3 states -- it builds its key set from the two counties' own records, so a stage present in either county appears with missing_a/missing_b set (the probe shows it) -- but a county with NO records at all contributes no key, so asking about it returned ZERO ROWS, and zero rows reads as 'nothing to report' rather than 'this county cannot be compared yet'. The question the table exists for is literally asked while Burnet has not run. Fixed by building the pair from the counties that were ASKED about, returning coverage/comparable, and exiting 4 from the CLI on an incomparable pair. That introduced a deliberate duplication of the ratio expressions between the function and the view, which is the paired-implementation shape DEV_PROCESS says drifts, so a live test asserts the two AGREE on a pair where both counties have data. (2) MY COMPLETENESS SWEEP WAS BLIND AND ITS FIRST GREEN WAS NOT EVIDENCE. The stage-map test matched only `phase: "literal"` and went green over 40 phases. SEVENTEEN assignment sites in src/ name their phase through a const (`phase: JOB_ID` with `const JOB_ID = "..."`), so sixteen live phases were invisible to it -- the guard was bypassed by writing a job the way seventeen existing jobs already are. Resolving the consts surfaced all sixteen; fifteen carry a stage read off their own header (quoted into the entry and marked provisional: true), one is DECLINED as a verification check that fills no rail, and one could not be read off the code at all, so PHASE_UNASSIGNED exists rather than a guessed stage number that the per-stage cost roll-up would then report as fact. (3) MY CHANGE BROKE TWO EXISTING TESTS AND THEY WERE RIGHT. The two depth-writer tests drove the jobs with a blanket `{ query: async () => ({ rows: [] }) }` double, which is not a model of `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id`: an empty row set is indistinguishable from a conflict, so a successful write looked like a duplicate and the run refused. I strengthened the doubles to answer the three statements the writer runs and to assert the record is opened exactly once and closed, rather than weakening the writer's conflict detection to suit a fake.

LESSON: A per-county number cannot come from a per-run row when the writer SWEEPS counties. Count the split where the writer knows it (inside the page loop, from the rows the UPDATE returned) rather than dividing the run's total by its scope list -- the scope list is a guess dressed as a denominator, and it would have poisoned the exact comparison the table exists to make.

The three-state rule has to be a CHECK in the schema, not a convention in the writer: the writer is the thing that would be wrong. A measured zero stays legal (>= 0 AND a basis), an absence carries a reason, and every other combination is refused by PostgreSQL.

A job cannot price its own execution while it is still running: the billable-instance-time series is not published until the execution ends. The honest state is a NAMED absence (METRIC_NOT_YET_PUBLISHED) that a later pass backfills, not a zero and not a guess.

`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id` returning no rows is ambiguous to a reader (conflict OR nothing happened). Read the identity back and, if the read also finds nothing, refuse with 'the store did not answer the write' -- inferring a conflict from an absence is the silent-fallback defect class this program hunts.

A comparison built on a view can only compare what the view can SEE. Joining two counties through their own records means a county with no records produces zero rows, which reads as 'nothing to report'. If the question is 'does A beat B yet', build the pair from the names you were ASKED about and return an explicit incomparable flag.

A test that sweeps the source for a pattern must resolve the ways the codebase actually writes that pattern. A `phase: "literal"` sweep missed SEVENTEEN `phase: CONST` sites, which is the majority shape of a phase assignment in this repo: the guard was bypassed by writing a new job the ordinary way. Its green was 'I looked at a subset', not 'there is nothing there'.
A sweep must also not read PROSE. The stage-map module's own doc block quotes the pattern the sweep searches for, and the first widened run demanded a stage number for a sentence.
Test doubles must model the SQL they are asked to run. A blanket `{ rows: [] }` fake is not a model of RETURNING, and adapting the CODE to suit that fake would have removed real duplicate-detection.
DEAD-END: Cost columns on `runs`. Wrong grain (one run per process invocation, many counties per run) and no way to carry a CHECK on the stage enum, a per-stage ended_at, or the three states.
Cost on `termination_records`. It records WHY a run ended, is written by a different actor at a different time, and would make a run's stage numbers depend on its ending cleanly.
Reading the comparison from stage_run_comparison when the caller has named two counties. Correct for a stage present in one county, silent for a county with no records at all.
A synthetic `runs` row for a dry run. It would put a never-run execution where the reaper reads, and make the audit wait for a run that will never end.
A `phase: "literal"`-only completeness sweep. Seventeen real assignment sites escape it.
